title: Rahab of Jericho
lead: The Canaanite woman of Jericho who hid Israel's spies, confessed the LORD, and was saved with her family. The New Testament names her among Jesus' ancestors and among the heroes of faith (Joshua 2; 6:22–25; Matthew 1:5; Hebrews 11:31; James 2:25).

sections.b: Joshua tells her story in two parts: her rescue of the spies and her confession of faith (Joshua 2), and her rescue with her family when Jericho fell (Joshua 6:22–25). Matthew lists her as the mother of Boaz in the line of David and Jesus (Matthew 1:5), one of four women in that genealogy, with Tamar, Ruth and Bathsheba. Hebrews 11:31 says that by faith she did not die with the disobedient, and James 2:25 says she was justified by works when she welcomed the messengers. The Rahab of Psalm 89:10 and Isaiah 51:9 is a different word, the name of a sea monster.
